title: Uptime Budget Record
body:
Overview

This is Manon's original Signature counterpart for Uptime Budget Record inside the Platform Reliability and Availability Signature Database, built as part of the Signature ecosystem rather than copied from any outside source. Models uptime, failure rates, repair times and maintenance needs. The Signature edition keeps the same discipline as the public edition: every entry states the task, shows the method in full, and carries a demo program that was genuinely executed at build time, so the result shown is a result that actually ran. Signature records are labeled as Signature originals wherever they appear, and they never present a design as an established fact. A design is called a design, a measured result is called a measured result, and the difference is kept visible in the record itself.

How it works

The method in each record is arithmetic on observed history: failures over operating time give a failure rate, repair durations give a repair time, and the two combine into availability. Models are only as good as their inputs, so each record states its observation window and its sample size alongside the result.

Worked detail

The worked detail for this Signature entry is concrete and reproducible. The accompanying demo program ran at build time and its output begins with: mean time between failures hours: 410. The complete program and its full output travel with this record, so any reader can re-run the code and confirm the result independently. The Signature version adapts the public method to Signature conventions: the same checks, the same honesty about limits, and the same requirement that a claim travel no further than its evidence. Where this entry describes a procedure, the steps are ordered and checkable; where it describes a model, the inputs, the calculation, and the uncertainty are all stated; where it describes a plan, the constraints are named first, because a plan that hides its constraints cannot be trusted when conditions change.

Use and ladder

A sustainment planner uses these records to set maintenance intervals, to size spares, and to judge whether a platform can meet its availability target with the maintenance it actually receives. Teaching ladder: this record is ranked simple. Simple Signature records introduce one idea at a time, compounded records combine ideas into a working procedure, and most-complex records carry the full procedure with its edge cases and limits. Feasibility tier: established. Implementation status: established. When the status is designed, this record offers a design plus an executed demo; deployment is not claimed. The Signature edition stands alongside the public edition as Manon's own original counterpart, and both editions are linked from the database page so readers can compare them.
demo_code:
# Uptime Budget Record: compute availability from failure and repair history.
mtbf_hours = 410
mttr_hours = 3
availability = mtbf_hours / (mtbf_hours + mttr_hours)
print("mean time between failures hours:", mtbf_hours)
print("mean time to repair hours:", mttr_hours)
print("availability:", round(availability, 5))
print("expected downtime hours per year:", round((1 - availability) * 8760, 1))
demo_output:
mean time between failures hours: 410
mean time to repair hours: 3
availability: 0.99274
expected downtime hours per year: 63.6
